The visible patch excerpt is truncated: it shows one row, DARKBLOOM_CBV2_SOLO_PREFILL_STRIPE, replaced by a DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK row (positive tokens, family policy, e.g. 2048 for GPT-OSS). The head excerpt starts at line 1 and stops at line 352, so the edited rows at 379-381 were not directly viewable on the head side. The base excerpt starts at 507. I could not verify the replaced text beyond the patch excerpt.

No code, auth, attestation, encryption or coordinator contract change is visible. A documentation-only change to a prefill tuning variable cannot alter A-001 (prompts), A-003 (X25519 key) or the prefix-cache posture in T-041 through this file. The visible configuration text keeps the existing security statements. The SSD prefix-cache TTL is at most 1800 s, and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_TTL_SECONDS can only shorten it. Cache storage is constrained by the volume-UUID check. The ephemeral-key and debug-key-file paths are non-release or test-only. The App Attest worker flag is exact-1 and is not production-ready. Endpoint resumption grants no local trust. Logout follows the stop-before-delete and issuer-bound contract. All of these are unchanged, consistent with the threat-model entries (T-041, T-053, T-057), and are not regressions.

Remaining question: if the renamed variable is a new runtime control, the real code change is in other files outside this batch. Integration should check whether the new prefill-chunk setting affects memory admission, DoS/resource bounds (T-010, T-029) or LaunchAgent passthrough, and whether the docs match the code. That is unverified here and is not a finding.
